title: Improved service for super? You’ll pay
full_text:
Millions of Australians will be slugged with higher rates for superannuation services as the nation’s largest fund lifts its administration fees.
In an update to its more than 3.6 million members, AustralianSuper said it was increasing the administration for the first time since 2022.
As part of the changes, from October 31, the administration fee for accumulation members will lift from 0.10 per cent to 0.12 per cent. For people with a balance up to $50,000, this is expected to cost about 49c more a week. For 88 per cent of accumulation members, representing about 3.1 million members with balances up to $250,000, administration fees will increase by up to $1.83 per week. Members with a bigger balance of $350,000-$500,000 or above will be asked to pay $5.97 more per week.
The administration fee cap for accumulation members has also increased from $350 to $600 per year.
AustralianSuper deputy chief executive Rose Kerlin said the higher fees would help the fund provide simpler, safe and more personalised experiences for members.
“We have brought more member-facing services in-house, strengthened account security, expanded access to advice and guidance services, and enhanced the digital tools members use to engage with their super,” Ms Kerlin said.
“These investments are helping us provide simpler, safer and more personalised experiences for members, and they are working.” Ms Kerlin said customer satisfaction scores were the highest they had ever been, while waiting times for call centres had been reduced to less than two minutes, with plans to keep improving.
However, Super Consumer Australia research found AustralianSuper failed to answer 90 per cent of calls during a mystery shopper study. This study was based on 20 major super fund call centres, with overall customer service found to be inconsistent, unclear and often short of basic expectations.
AustralianSuper disputes these claims, saying the survey was taken more than a year ago and it had since transitioned to a new call centre provider.
No super fund in the study performed well.
Super Consumers Australia chief executive Xavier O’Halloran called for all funds, including AustralianSuper, to lift their game when it came to customer service. “People don’t just need a healthy super balance to have a dignified retirement. They need to know their fund will pick up the phone when they’re grieving, need to access their money or ask a simple question and actually help them,” he said.
AustralianSuper told members they should expect further improvements in cyber security, with industry-leading verification tools coming online soon.
“We remain committed to managing costs carefully, investing for the long term and delivering the support, products and performance our members need to build their best retirement,’ Ms Kerlin said. “As a profit-to-member fund, every dollar we collect in fees is used to operate and strengthen the fund on behalf of members.”
